summary.headline: CMR Green Q1 FY27 revenue rose 65% YoY to INR3,122 crore and PAT 22% to INR68 crore, with EBITDA/kg at about INR12.40 but operating cash flow negative.
summary.overview: Revenue from operations grew 65% YoY to INR3,122 crore, EBITDA rose 27% to INR139 crore and PAT rose 22% to over INR68 crore, with aluminium volumes up 25% YoY. Management stressed EBITDA per kg (about INR12.40) over percentage margin because aluminium is largely a pass-through. Operating cash flow was negative due to a roughly 40% rise in average realisation (from about INR226-230/kg to INR350/kg), which raised working capital; inventory days fell to 40 from 45 and the cash conversion cycle to 65 days from 69. Management kept INR12/kg EBITDA and 25% FY27 volume growth as internal targets, while the Odisha plant ramps up.

segments.name: Aluminium (recycled alloys/ingots and liquid metal)
segments.commentary: Aluminium volumes grew 32% YoY in Q1; liquid aluminium now exceeds 50% of aluminium sales, and management expects liquid metal growth to outpace ingot growth. Liquid metal margins are higher but management did not quantify the gap.

segments.name: Recycled billets and UBC
segments.commentary: Billets volume +149% YoY and UBC volume +333% YoY, both in ramp-up mode. Management cites construction, renewables, electrical and industrial demand beyond automotive.

segments.name: Non-ferrous (other metals) mix
segments.commentary: Aluminium to other non-ferrous sales mix held at about 80:20. FY26 volume mix was 66% automotive alloys, 10% non-automotive and 24% other metals; target rebalancing to 60:20:20 over the coming year.

guidance_outlook: Internal target of 25% volume growth in FY27, which management says is based on Tirupati and Odisha ramp-up, brownfield expansion and existing auto customers.
EBITDA guidance held at INR12/kg on a sustainable basis; management said it could do better but is not guiding above that.
Installed recycling capacity to exceed 7 lakh tons per annum by end FY27 (about 6.15 lakh tons currently), per management.
Expects to reach full utilisation at the Odisha (Hindalco) plant within FY27; current run-rate about 6,000 tons for the quarter, targeting about 4,000 tons a month.
Expects to return to positive operating cash flow once aluminium prices stabilise; debt to fall as inventory days and working capital cycle reduce.
Plans to bring debt-equity back toward its historical 0.5 ratio; currently about 0.86.
capex_capacity: INR53 crore invested in the quarter in greenfield projects at Shoolagiri and Bawal, with brownfield and technology projects at Tirupati and other locations progressing as planned.
Odisha plant (48,000 tpa capacity, built for Hindalco) is ramping up.
Capacity utilisation is about 65%; traditional range of 70-75%.
Hindustan Zinc: MoU signed, nothing definitive, and no construction started; management says it will take a while.
demand_pricing: Passenger vehicle and two-wheeler sales grew about 26% and 20% YoY in Q1 FY27; EV penetration was 8.26% of registrations in FY26. Ather Energy is a new customer.
Auto customers are on cost-plus pricing; management says hedging is used to manage the balance on the un-passed-through portion.
Exports were about 3.4% of FY26 turnover, focused on niche products to Japan, Europe, Southeast Asia and some China.
Management says volumes are independent of aluminium price movements; scrap availability is not price-dependent.
Management says scrap sourcing is getting harder as some countries restrict scrap exports; the company is widening its sourcing base and buying more domestically.

Regulatory tailwinds: proposed EPR framework to lift minimum recycled aluminium content from 5% in FY28 to 10% over time; EU CBAM cited; India's aluminium extrusion industry expected to grow at 12% CAGR through FY29.
Recycled aluminium is about 40% of India's aluminium consumption, growing about 13% a year versus about 7-8% for primary, per management.

qa_highlights.question: How does hedging work for secondary aluminium given peers say it cannot be hedged?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said secondary prices follow primary with a lag and auto customers pay cost-plus, so part of exposure is left to cost-plus pricing and part is hedged on LME. The CFO added that operating cash flow is negative because average realisation rose about 40%, from INR226-230/kg to INR350/kg.

qa_highlights.question: Why did other expenses rise about 20% QoQ?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said INR36 crore was loaded for a cash flow hedge entry under accounting standards, not a hedging cost; other expenses were broadly flat QoQ.

qa_highlights.question: Will operating cash flow turn positive and what will debt be by year-end?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects positive operating cash flow once prices stabilise. The CFO said D/E is about 0.86 against a historical 0.5 target, which should fall as prices stabilise.

qa_highlights.question: Why does reported EBITDA differ from the earlier presentation for Q4 and FY26?
qa_highlights.answer: The CFO said the company reclassified foreign exchange gains and the ineffective portion of commodity hedging from other income into EBITDA as they are operating in nature, though accounting standards require other-income classification.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 25% FY27 volume growth still on track after Q1 aluminium volume growth of about 8%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said 25% is an internal target, not guidance; Q1 volume grew 25%, and growth is expected from the Tirupati and Odisha plants and existing customers.

qa_highlights.question: Do GP and EBITDA per kg move with utilisation, and how should hedging costs be treated?
qa_highlights.answer: Management held INR12/kg EBITDA as guidance despite utilisation of about 65% versus 70-75% historical. It said hedging costs are minimal (broker and LME fees) and that hedging works against physical profit or loss.

risks_watch: Operating cash flow negative in Q1 FY27 as average realisation rose about 40% (INR226-230/kg to INR350/kg); management ties return to positive OCF to price stabilisation, with no timeline given.
Debt-equity about 0.86 versus the historical 0.5 target; management said debt should fall as inventory days and the cash conversion cycle reduce, but no year-end debt figure was given.

25% FY27 volume growth is an internal target, not guidance; Q1 aluminium volume growth was about 8% per an analyst's framing (management said Q1 total volume grew 25%), so the back-half ramp at Tirupati and Odisha must be tracked.

Odisha (Hindalco, 48,000 tpa) must reach about 4,000 tons a month from about 6,000 tons for the quarter to hit full utilisation within FY27; Hindustan Zinc MoU has no definitive agreement or construction start.
Scrap sourcing is getting harder as some countries restrict scrap exports; the company is widening its supply base and buying more domestically.

Hedging of secondary aluminium relies on a balance between cost-plus auto pricing and LME hedges; the INR36 crore cash flow hedge entry in other expenses and the reclassification of FX and commodity hedge ineffectiveness from other income into adjusted EBITDA affect comparability with prior presentations.
key_quotes: So in this quarter earning and also in future we may see that the EBITDA as a percentage has gone up or gone down. That should not be taken as a real measure of our performance.
The 25% is our definitely our internal targets.
Look, sourcing of scrap is getting challenging. There are countries which are putting restrictions on export of scrap from those countries.
We could do better maybe but for guidance we will maintain it at INR12.
summary.management_tone: Management was confident on volumes, pricing discipline and the regulatory outlook, but cautious and sometimes evasive on forward numbers: it declined to build expectations beyond the 25% internal volume target, held EBITDA at INR12/kg despite saying it could do better, and did not quantify the liquid metal margin premium or the hedging accounting entry.

adds.what: Installed recycling capacity to exceed 7 lakh tpa (from about 6.15 lakh tpa) via Shoolagiri, Bawal, Tirupati and other projects
Odisha (Hindalco-built) 48,000 tpa plant ramping up to full utilisation within FY27
Hindustan Zinc MoU, no definitive agreement and no construction started

growth.why: Management targets 25% FY27 volume growth (internal target, Q1 revenue up 65% on higher aluminium prices), backed by Odisha ramp-up and capacity going above 7 lakh tpa by end FY27, but utilisation is only about 65% and the Hindustan Zinc project has not started.
